name: Many Peaks - Intro Walk
description:
***THIS WALK IS AT CAPACITY** 
𝐖𝐞 𝐝𝐨 𝐧𝐨𝐭 𝐚𝐜𝐜𝐞𝐩𝐭 𝐑𝐒𝐕𝐏𝐬 𝐯𝐢𝐚 𝐅𝐚𝐜𝐞𝐛𝐨𝐨𝐤'𝐬 "𝐆𝐨𝐢𝐧𝐠" 𝐟𝐞𝐚𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞. 𝐖𝐞 𝐝𝐨 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐛𝐞𝐜𝐚𝐮𝐬𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐛 𝐥𝐢𝐦𝐢𝐭𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐢𝐫 𝐠𝐫𝐨𝐮𝐩 𝐭𝐨 𝟏𝟐-𝟏𝟓 𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐢𝐜𝐢𝐩𝐚𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐦𝐚𝐱 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐅𝐁 𝐝𝐨𝐞𝐬 𝐧𝐨𝐭 𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐨𝐰 𝐮𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐝𝐨 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐭. 

Many Peaks - Intro Walk
Leader: Molly

Rated- Level 2. You should have at least attempted Castle Hill. This is not for the absolute beginner , mainly due to the heat and time this walk will take.

Duration (approx) of walking per day - Approximately 4 hours. 2km circuit.
If you have RSVPd via the form(not "Going" on FB) you will have received an email about the meeting place and time. 𝐖𝐞 𝐝𝐨 𝐧𝐨𝐭 𝐚𝐜𝐜𝐞𝐩𝐭 𝐑𝐒𝐕𝐏𝐬 𝐯𝐢𝐚 𝐅𝐚𝐜𝐞𝐛𝐨𝐨𝐤'𝐬 "𝐆𝐨𝐢𝐧𝐠" 𝐟𝐞𝐚𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞. 𝐖𝐞 𝐝𝐨 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐛𝐞𝐜𝐚𝐮𝐬𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐛 𝐥𝐢𝐦𝐢𝐭𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐢𝐫 𝐠𝐫𝐨𝐮𝐩 𝐭𝐨 𝟏𝟐-𝟏𝟓 𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐢𝐜𝐢𝐩𝐚𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐦𝐚𝐱 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐅𝐁 𝐝𝐨𝐞𝐬 𝐧𝐨𝐭 𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐨𝐰 𝐮𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐝𝐨 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐭. 

About the walk:
On this hike we'll be heading up Lagoon trail and walking along this flat trail for about 2 kms or so before taking the turn off and making our way up the Many Peaks trail to the Mount Marlow summit. We'll take a few short stops along the way, and we will take a break at the top to take in the views. We will then come down Mt Marlow.

Approximate Time/Distance: 3-4 hours return , 12km circuit.
What to expect: Moderate level of fitness required. Expect some steep, uneven and rocky sections.

There are exposed sections, so expect it to be hot. I cannot reiterate this enough - Bring plenty of hydration.

The pace will be moderate and continuous, so we can cover the distance within the designated time-frame and enjoy our stops at the points of interest mentioned.


What to bring on the walk - https://bit.ly/wtbdayhike


Information and maps for the Townsville Town Common Conservation Park:
https://wanderstories.space/cape-pallarenda/
https://parks.des.qld.gov.au/parks/townsville/

name: Remote waterfalls near the Herbert River / Wallaman
description:
Wallaman / Herbert River Area
Leader: Luen

This off-track adventure is rated very hard (5), and a good level of fitness is essential. The hike will take us through some rugged terrain, including rock hopping, wet and slippery rocks, and uneven ground. Since we'll be camping overnight, a QPWS camping permit is required.

We’ll start with a couple of kilometres along a track before ascending a ridgeline, eventually descending into a creek to visit a remote waterfall where we'll set up camp. As flat ground is unlikely, hammock camping is recommended – even a budget hammock from Bunnings will do.

Total distance: approximately 13km on day one, with a weekend total of around 25km. On the return, we’ll either take the same route or rock hop down the creek back to the track and out to the cars. Please carry enough water for the ascent, as it will be a full day of hiking on both days. Day one is more challenging, starting at an elevation of 60m and climbing up to 300m.

Luen will email the GPX route and meeting details to those who have registered closer to the event.

Gear Notes:
Hammock (recommended for camping)
Secateurs (for cutting through vines and vegetation)

Email the walk leader for more information luenwarneke@gmail.com
